title: Separate the variables
text: Separate to get $$\frac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\ln\left(t\right) dt$$ and notice that the left side integrates to $$\arcsin{x}$$

title: Integrate and solve
text: Integration by parts gives $$t \ln\left(t\right)-t$$ for the right side, so $$\arcsin{x}=t\ln(t)-t+C$$ and at $$t=1$$, $$x=0$$ this gives $$C=1$$. So $$x=sin\left(t \ln\left(t\right)-t+1\right)$$.
